conviction_note: Hooker filed ~$8m of IEEPA tariff refund claims in fiscal Q1 and deliberately withheld the number from the earnings call, disclosing it only inside the 10-Q's 'Tariff Update' section; CBP paid out the bulk of IEEPA refunds during exactly the May-Aug window this quarter covers and the closest comparable furniture importer (Ethan Allen) banked $5.0m of cash refunds by 30 June, so recognition of $6-8m pre-tax (~$0.55-0.75/share on 10.7m shares, ~6% of a $133m cap) against a ($0.02) consensus is more likely than not and is not in a stock that has drifted down 16.6% in 20 days on 35k shares a day.

findings.finding: Hooker submitted approximately $8 million of IEEPA tariff refund claims during fiscal Q1 (ended 3 May 2026) and recognised none of it, applying a gain-contingency model that books the benefit only when cash is realised — the amount appears only in the 10-Q's 'Tariff Update' section, and $8m pre-tax is ~6% of the $133m market cap and ~$0.75/share pre-tax on 10.7m shares against a ($0.02) consensus.
findings.why_not_priced: On the 11 June call CFO Earl Armstrong was asked directly for the rebate number by an investor and answered 'we have decided not to disclose that publicly, at least on the call', pointing instead to 'some additional disclosure in the queue' — so every wire story, transcript summary and screen-driven investor got the quarter without the number, and only a reader of the 10-Q body has it. If the market had priced a windfall worth 6% of the cap the stock would not be making 20-day lows (-16.6%) with turnover at $0.4m/day into the print, and the ($0.02) consensus would not sit where a refund puts GAAP EPS at +$0.50 or better. There is no sell-side note, no 8-K and no press release carrying the $8m figure.
findings.independence: Ethan Allen, a directly comparable US furniture importer, disclosed it actually received $5.0m of IEEPA tariff refund cash inside its quarter ended 30 June 2026 — inside Hooker's 4 May-2 Aug window: https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/07/30/tmt-newswire/globenewswire/ethan-allen-reports-fiscal-2026-full-year-and-fourth-quarter-results-strong-margins-and-robust-balance-sheet-despite-macroeconomic-challenges-declares-special-and-regular-cash-dividend/2394422 (2026-07-30). Separately, CAPE refund tracking shows ~$106.6bn of IEEPA refunds completed and sent to Treasury as of 21 Aug 2026, with June 2026 the largest payout month: https://www.tariffstool.com/cape-refund-status (as-of 2026-08-29). Both are different documents from the 10-Q.

findings.finding: Industry wholesale order data covering Hooker's actual quarter is running well ahead of the 'weak housing' narrative: Smith Leonard's survey of residential furniture manufacturers shows May 2026 new orders +8% y/y with backlogs +5%, and June 2026 new orders $2.26bn +11% y/y with backlogs $2.64bn +11% y/y and H1 orders +4% — against Hooker's own disclosed May orders +8% and backlog +14% y/y.
findings.why_not_priced: Smith Leonard is a High Point accounting firm's monthly survey with no ticker attached and no wire pickup; the June-data edition only reached trade press on 8 Sep 2026, three days before the print. The wire narrative on HOFT is uniformly 'weak housing, cautious consumer', and if manufacturer-level order acceleration were priced the stock would not have de-rated 16.6% in 20 days while the industry's own backlog was up 11% y/y. I size this small deliberately because the ($0.31)-to-($0.02) improvement is already consensus.
findings.independence: Cuts partly the other way and I am flagging it rather than hiding it: Ethan Allen reported wholesale written orders -11.9% and retail written orders -10.8% in the June quarter (https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/07/30/tmt-newswire/globenewswire/ethan-allen-reports-fiscal-2026-full-year-and-fourth-quarter-results-strong-margins-and-robust-balance-sheet-despite-macroeconomic-challenges-declares-special-and-regular-cash-dividend/2394422) and La-Z-Boy's FY27 Q1 (ended 25 Jul 2026) showed sales -3% with GAAP EPS $(0.06) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/57131/000005713126000034/fy27q1pressrelease.htm). Those are retail/own-brand written demand; Smith Leonard is wholesale shipments and backlog, which is Hooker's model — hence the small net positive and the wide band. NOTE: this finding shares the Ethan Allen document with finding 1; the refund fact and the order fact are different lines of that release.

findings.finding: An 8-K filed 4 September 2026 (event date 26 August, eight days before the print) discloses that the Compensation Committee found CEO Jeremy Hoff's equity awards had exceeded the plan's 75,000-share annual limit in two consecutive years — by 46,149 shares for fiscal 2026 and 31,968 shares for fiscal 2027 — and rescinded and cancelled the excess PSUs, adding 'enhanced controls'.
findings.why_not_priced: It was filed into a quiet period on a $133m-cap name with no analyst coverage and generated zero wire pickup — a search of HOFT news for August-September 2026 surfaces only the earnings-date notice and the dividend. If the market had read it there would be at least one governance headline and a Form 4 amendment cluster in the press. Small by construction: it is a controls blemish and a two-year mis-grant, not a cash item, and the cancellation is mildly anti-dilutive.

searched_and_found_nothing: The sweep's Home Meridian angle is stale — HMI's Pulaski and Samuel Lawrence brands were already sold to Magnussen and the segment no longer appears in the fiscal 2027 segment table (Hooker Branded / Domestic Upholstery / All Other); there is no pending exit decision left to surprise on.

The FY2026 $25m annualised cost-reduction target: the company has already reported $17.5m of fixed-cost reduction achieved in the prior year and the SG&A delivery is visible in the Q1 gross-margin bridge (+440bp), so there is no quantifiable undisclosed delivery gap I could establish.
The 3 September dividend at $0.115 is simply the maintenance of the recalibrated $0.46 annual rate set from 31 December 2025 — no change, no information.
Section 232 wood/upholstered furniture tariff rates: the scheduled 1 Jan 2026 step-ups to 30%/50% were delayed to at least 2027, which is public and widely covered — no edge.
Insider activity: the June/July 2026 Form 4s I checked are routine RSU grants (e.g. Richard L. Vest II, 4,454 RSUs, 1 July 2026, code A), not open-market purchases; no Form 4 buy cluster.
No 8-K, press release, wire story or sell-side note anywhere carrying the $8m refund figure — searched '"Hooker Furnishings" tariff refund "$8 million"' and HOFT August/September 2026 news.
No usable option chain, so no skew or implied move to test the finding against.
Could not establish HOFT-specific short interest or a live buyback authorisation from a dated primary source.
baseline_tension: It cuts hard against the tape — the stock is down 16.6% in 20 days and 30% off its 52-week high, and the one thing the market cannot see from the call transcript or the wire is an $8m cash claim worth ~6% of the market cap that peers with coterminous quarters have already banked; with no option chain there is no skew to agree or disagree with, so the only priced statement is the drift, and this contradicts it.
